newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes dip in Asia after API data shows stock rise.
newsitem.headline: Crudes dip in Asia after API data shows stock rise.

text.p: Crude oil prices inched down in Asia on Wednesday after the weekly API data showed a bearish increase in gasoline and oil stocks, while activity in the physical market remained thin, traders said.
June cash Brent was notionally assessed at $18.00/18.05 per barrel in late Tokyo trading, mostly unchanged throughout the day and down about five cents from late U.S. trading levels.
"It's the API data that's behind it," one broker said.
The latest API figures showed that gasoline stocks had increased by 3.6 million barrels to 199.6 barrels in the week ended April 11.
U.S. crude oil stocks held in primary storage rose 2.97 million barrels to 311.41 million barrels.
In Brent/Dubai spreads June was notionally assessed at $1.30/1.35 a touch narrower than overnight levels due to Brent's weakness.
In the physical market, a Japanese trader confirmed that it had sold a June Masila cargo at a premium of 12 to 13 cents to a major.
Discussion in other Gulf crudes remained dull with many potential buyers relaxed on expectations the market for June-loading cargoes would probably remain weak.

A total of 600,000 barrels of April Al Shaheen was rumoured to have been sold by a Danish company to a South Korean refiner. One trader said he believed the deal had been done at a discount of $2 to C&F Dubai quotes, while some others thought that the deal had been done at a sharper discount.

In Asian crudes, some traders said they had heard that China had purchased altogether 600,000 barrels of May Widuri and Cinta crudes. The Cinta was believed to have been sold at a premium of about five cents to ICP, while the Widuri sold at a slightly higher premium. -- M.Yoshikawa, Tokyo +81-3-5473-3706
